decisions.reason: Launched with its own page as a new product line, Product A shows high public commitment and strategic centrality, so escalation of commitment makes persistence likely.

Although only mentioned on the website, Product B builds on the established offer and represents meaningful investment, so the firm tends to persist while results can be attributed to temporary causes.

Product C is a support tool that builds on the established offer but has only a website mention, indicating moderate commitment; under escalation, the firm is likely to continue it absent clear permanent failure.
Presented on its own page and building on the established offer, Product D reflects substantial investment and public commitment, making early withdrawal less likely under escalation of commitment.
As a complete bundle close to the established offer with its own page, Product E signals strong commitment and integration with the firm's announced direction, favoring persistence.
Product F is distant from the established offer and only mentioned, implying little investment and low public commitment, so escalation theory predicts dropping it is easier to justify.
